events.title: Git created
events.summary: Linus Torvalds committed the first revision of Git on April 7, 2005 — a distributed version control system for the Linux [kernel].
events.about: Git stores snapshots and branches locally, merges with three-way diffs, and syncs via push/pull to remotes. Every open-source project, GitHub workflow, and CI pipeline depends on it. Example: feature branch → commit → pull request → merge to main — all Git operations under the hood.

narrative.whyChosen: Git replaced BitKeeper for [kernel] development and became the world's default VCS.
narrative.whyImportant: Distributed history, cheap branching, and SHA-1 object storage changed how teams collaborate on code.
narrative.problemSolved: Centralized VCS could not match Linux's scale; Torvalds needed fast distributed merges after BitKeeper's license ended.

events.title: Mercurial released
events.summary: Matt Mackall announced Mercurial v0.1 on April 19, 2005 — a distributed version control system born after BitKeeper's free license ended.
events.about: Mercurial (`hg`) stores changesets with efficient delta compression and supports clone/branch/pull workflows like Git. Mozilla, Facebook, and Python used it before Git dominated. Bitbucket built on Mercurial for years. Example: `hg clone`, edit, `hg commit`, `hg push` to a central or peer repo.

narrative.whyChosen: Mercurial was Git's main rival in the 2005 distributed VCS race after BitKeeper withdrew.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved multiple DVCS designs could work at scale and kept competition alive during the Git adoption wave.
narrative.problemSolved: Linux [kernel] developers needed a free distributed SCM when BitKeeper's license was revoked.
